# What the subagent's session digest turned out to be

SEEN-105 designed the `subagent` disclosure around a reviewer_session the
spawning session records, and its own journal at record 7 observed that a Claude
Code subagent inherits its parent's session id. This ticket measured it directly.
The reviewer agent was asked to run
`python3 -c "from harness import sessions; print(sessions.current())"` in its own
context and returned `253bf8e84e82`, which is the digest on every record this
session has written on SEEN-107.

So on Claude Code the harness cannot tell a review that ran in a subagent's own
context from one the parent wrote, because there is nothing in the environment
that differs. `_require_another_context` would refuse the honest value, and the
only value that would pass is one nobody measured, which is what the skill
already says it cannot detect.

This review is therefore disclosed as `self-review`, which is what the harness's
own vocabulary means by it: the session that wrote the code is the session the
review came from, by the only identifier either has. It understates what
happened. The review did run in a context of its own, with its own tool budget,
that had not read this code; it returned five findings, three of which became
code. The word that describes that is `subagent`, and it is unavailable on this
assistant for want of a distinguishable identifier.

Recorded rather than worked around. SEEN-105's fourth criterion rests on a
distinction this platform does not currently expose, and the ticket that wants it
back needs either a Codex reviewer, where the contexts are separate processes, or
an identifier the spawning session mints and passes into the task, which would be
a declaration and not a measurement.
